sermon.title: Essential for Diplomacy
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing the series on adding patience to faith, the speaker says patience is essential for diplomats of Bible morality. He points to the prophets and Job (James 5:10), rewards for patiently doing good (Romans 2:6), waiting for Christ’s return (James 5:7), recognizing true Christians (Revelation 2–3; 14:12), and a gentle, teaching response to humanism (2 Timothy 2:24), then argues Congress has established secular humanism and that Johnson’s 501(c)(3) gag order violates the First Amendment.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Caption corrections include “Revelation” for “Revelations,” “Smyrna” for “Samaria,” “abridging” for “a bridge in,” “unrighteousness” for “on righteousness,” “13:10” for “13 9” (wording matches Revelation 13:10), “humanists” for “human is,” and “today” for “to death” (“he isn’t coming today”). He cites many statistics (STD rates, alcohol deaths, divorce, poverty, wars, suicides, 1400 churches) without naming sources—flagged for Michael, not verified here. Sensitive political and social claims kept as spoken. Speaker not named in the recording; attributed as Pastor David G. Kincer in series continuity—confirm.

chunks.section_question: What do the prophets and Job teach about patience?
chunks.short_answer: He reads James 5:10 that the prophets are an example of patience in suffering and are counted blessed because they endured without complaining or losing their temper. He says Job was perfect and upright (Job 31), yet lost his children, wealth, and health.
chunks.text: And James 5:10, the Bible says that the prophets are an example of patience and suffering, and they’re counted blessed because they endured the patience and suffering without complaining and without losing their temper. Yeah. And then he says, you have heard of the patience of Job and the end result of the Lord. Now, Job is a perfect and upright man, and in Job 31 it tells us Job had no deceit, no sexual immorality, no going astray, no greed, no abusers of his employees. He didn’t mistreat orphans or the poor. He didn’t mistreat those that hated him. He had no secret sin. He was not afraid of the crowd. He lodged travelers. He was not silent about wrong. And yet he lost his children, his wealth, and his health.

scriptures.text_nkjv: My brethren, take the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord, as an example of suffering and patience.

“I have made a covenant with my eyes; Why then should I look upon a young woman? For what is the allotment of God from above, And the inheritance of the Almighty from on high? Is it not destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the workers of iniquity? Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps? “If I have walked with falsehood, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit, Let me be weighed on honest scales, That God may know my integrity. If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart walked after my eyes, Or if any spot adheres to my hands, Then let me sow, and another eat; Yes, let my harvest be rooted out. “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door, Then let my wife grind for another, And let others bow down over her. For that would be wickedness; Yes, it would be iniquity deserving of judgment. For that would be a fire that consumes to destruction, And would root out all my increase. “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant When they complained against me, What then shall I do when God rises up? When He punishes, how shall I answer Him? Did not He who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb? “If I have kept the poor from their desire, Or caused the eyes of the widow to fail, Or eaten my morsel by myself, So that the fatherless could not eat of it (But from my youth I reared him as a father, And from my mother’s womb I guided the widow); If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or any poor man without covering; If his heart has not blessed me, And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, When I saw I had help in the gate; Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, Let my arm be torn from the socket. For destruction from God is a terror to me, And because of His magnificence I cannot endure. “If I have made gold my hope, Or said to fine gold, ‘You are my confidence’; If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gained much; If I have observed the sun when it shines, Or the moon moving in brightness, So that my heart has been secretly enticed, And my mouth has kissed my hand; This also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, For I would have denied God who is above. “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, Or lifted myself up when evil found him (Indeed I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for a curse on his soul); If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ (But no sojourner had to lodge in the street, For I have opened my doors to the traveler); If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom, Because I feared the great multitude, And dreaded the contempt of families, So that I kept silence And did not go out of the door— Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my mark. Oh, that the Almighty would answer me, That my Prosecutor had written a book! Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, And bind it on me like a crown; I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him. “If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together; If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or caused its owners to lose their lives; Then let thistles grow instead of wheat, And weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

Farmers—and he gives this illustration—number one, wait for the precious fruit; number two, they wait for the fruit of the earth and they have long patience for it; number three, they’re patient until they receive the early, the spring rain, and the late summer rain. Be also patient and establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord draws nigh. The separation of church and state is a lie by humanists to silence Bible morality, Jesus, and his church. A lie repeated often enough is accepted as a truth. Thank you.

paragraphs.text: I submit to you today the churches have a right to peacefully assemble. They have a right to petition and request a remedy for our objections, and we have a right to speak out on our objections. Our Constitution gives us that right. And I submit to you this morning that Johnson’s gag order in the 501(c)(3) in 1954 violated the First Amendment when he added to the religious exemption that churches could not talk about political things and talk about political leaders. That is tyranny. That is wrong, and it violates the First Amendment. 1400 churches this October are defying this gag by announcing that they’re preaching politics in this month—1400 churches, yes—and they’re daring the humanist to take it to the Supreme Court because we’re sure we’re going to win. The separation of church and state is a lie by humanists to silence Bible morality, Jesus, and his church. A lie repeated often enough is accepted as a truth. Thank you.

faqs.question: What does he say we still have to add to our faith after salvation?
faqs.answer: He says when you got saved, filled with the Holy Spirit, or baptized in water you did not get these qualities—you still have to add them with the help of the Spirit, even though some are part of the fruit of the Spirit.

faqs.question: What does he say Job 31 shows about Job’s character?
faqs.answer: He says Job had no deceit, no sexual immorality, no going astray, no greed, did not mistreat employees, orphans, the poor, or those who hated him, had no secret sin, lodged travelers, and was not silent about wrong.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I have made a covenant with my eyes; Why then should I look upon a young woman? For what is the allotment of God from above, And the inheritance of the Almighty from on high? Is it not destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the workers of iniquity? Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps? “If I have walked with falsehood, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit, Let me be weighed on honest scales, That God may know my integrity. If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart walked after my eyes, Or if any spot adheres to my hands, Then let me sow, and another eat; Yes, let my harvest be rooted out. “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door, Then let my wife grind for another, And let others bow down over her. For that would be wickedness; Yes, it would be iniquity deserving of judgment. For that would be a fire that consumes to destruction, And would root out all my increase. “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant When they complained against me, What then shall I do when God rises up? When He punishes, how shall I answer Him? Did not He who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb? “If I have kept the poor from their desire, Or caused the eyes of the widow to fail, Or eaten my morsel by myself, So that the fatherless could not eat of it (But from my youth I reared him as a father, And from my mother’s womb I guided the widow); If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or any poor man without covering; If his heart has not blessed me, And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, When I saw I had help in the gate; Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, Let my arm be torn from the socket. For destruction from God is a terror to me, And because of His magnificence I cannot endure. “If I have made gold my hope, Or said to fine gold, ‘You are my confidence’; If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gained much; If I have observed the sun when it shines, Or the moon moving in brightness, So that my heart has been secretly enticed, And my mouth has kissed my hand; This also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, For I would have denied God who is above. “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, Or lifted myself up when evil found him (Indeed I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for a curse on his soul); If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ (But no sojourner had to lodge in the street, For I have opened my doors to the traveler); If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom, Because I feared the great multitude, And dreaded the contempt of families, So that I kept silence And did not go out of the door— Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my mark. Oh, that the Almighty would answer me, That my Prosecutor had written a book! Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, And bind it on me like a crown; I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him. “If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together; If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or caused its owners to lose their lives; Then let thistles grow instead of wheat, And weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

faqs.question: What does he say humanist faith believes?
faqs.answer: He says their self-seeking faith is that there is no God, no hell, no eternal life; the Bible is a myth full of errors; and human reasoning solves all human problems.

faqs.question: What is the farmer illustration in James 5:7?
faqs.answer: He says farmers wait for the precious fruit of the earth with long patience until they receive the early spring rain and the late summer rain, and believers should likewise be patient and establish their hearts because the Lord’s coming draws near.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore be patient, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently for it until it receives the early and latter rain. You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

faqs.question: What does he say about Hitler and Stalin?
faqs.answer: He says Hitler, Stalin, and many other bullies were all humanists and did terrible atrocities.

faqs.question: What does he say the church at Ephesus did with false apostles?
faqs.answer: He reads Revelation 2:2 that they could not bear those who are evil, tested those who said they were apostles and were not, and found them liars.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I know your works, your labor, your patience, and that you cannot bear those who are evil. And you have tested those who say they are apostles and are not, and have found them liars;

faqs.question: What is the patience of the saints in Revelation 14:12?
faqs.answer: He says it is those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus—that is the word of his patience, and you patiently do it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

faqs.question: What does he say Romans 13 and Genesis 9 teach about the sword?
faqs.answer: He says civil leaders are to use the sword to punish and correct evildoers, and that bullies who use the sword will perish by the sword.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God.
“Whoever sheds man’s blood, By man his blood shall be shed; For in the image of God He made man.

faqs.question: What attitude does 2 Timothy 2:24 require toward opponents?
faqs.answer: He says the servant of the Lord must not quarrel or debate just to be debating, but be gentle to all, teach, be patient, and in meekness instruct those who oppose themselves so God may give repentance.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel but be gentle to all, able to teach, patient, in humility correcting those who are in opposition, if God perhaps will grant them repentance, so that they may know the truth, and that they may come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his will.

faqs.question: What First Amendment rights does he say churches still have?
faqs.answer: He says the First Amendment protects free exercise of religion, freedom of speech and press, peaceable assembly, and petitioning government for redress of grievances, and that churches have a right to speak out on their objections.

faqs.question: What does he say about separation of church and state?
faqs.answer: He says separation of church and state is a lie by humanists to silence Bible morality, Jesus, and his church, and that a lie repeated often enough is accepted as a truth.

faqs.question: What does he say 1400 churches were doing that October?
faqs.answer: He says 1400 churches that October were defying the 501(c)(3) gag by announcing they were preaching politics that month, daring humanists to take it to the Supreme Court because they were sure they would win.
